## What OP-39 measures

**OP-39 — Breast Cancer Screening Recall Rates** reports the percentage of screening mammograms followed by diagnostic imaging within 45 days. Follow-up may include additional mammography, ultrasound, or MRI.

A recall can be a necessary part of screening, while unnecessary follow-up can add cost and anxiety. The rate alone cannot distinguish appropriate follow-up from avoidable callbacks, and it should not be treated as a stand-alone measure of a hospital's overall quality.

The charts below use hospitals with an available OP-39 score in the July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025 reporting period.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

imaging_url <- "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/sites/default/files/resources/d0134a9a89e59d49426cf5a2ad063b60_1792599881/Outpatient_Imaging_Efficiency-Hospital.csv"

mammography_scores <- read_csv(imaging_url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(`Measure ID` == "OP-39", Score != "Not Available") |>
  mutate(Score = as.numeric(Score))
```


## OP-39 at a Glance

These statistics summarize the reported breast screening recall percentages across hospitals. A recall means that additional diagnostic imaging followed a screening mammogram within 45 days.

```{r}
#| results: asis

mammo_stats <- mammography_scores |>
  summarise(
    hospitals = n_distinct(`Facility ID`),
    median_score = median(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(Score, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(Score, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat('<div class="imaging-stats">')

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%s</strong><span>Hospitals reporting OP-39</span></div>',
  format(mammo_stats$hospitals, big.mark = ",")
))

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%.1f%%</strong><span>Median breast screening recall rate</span></div>',
  mammo_stats$median_score
))

cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="imaging-stat"><strong>%.1f%%–%.1f%%</strong><span>Middle 50%% of hospital scores</span></div>',
  mammo_stats$q25,
  mammo_stats$q75
))

cat('</div>')
```

### Understanding Recall Rates

A screening mammogram may identify an area that requires further examination. In these cases, a patient may be called back for additional mammography, ultrasound, or other diagnostic imaging.

Recall rates matter because unnecessary callbacks can create anxiety, extra appointments, and additional costs. However, follow-up imaging can also be essential for investigating suspicious findings.

**A lower recall rate is not automatically better.** Interpreting these percentages requires clinical context, including the patients being screened and the reasons for additional imaging.

---

## Distribution across hospitals

Each bar counts reporting hospitals in a score range. Explore the shape of the distribution, but remember that the reported percentage is not a direct measure of cancer detection or patient outcomes.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = mammography_scores,
  x = ~Score,
  type = "histogram",
  xbins = list(size = 1.5),
  marker = list(color = "#d87850")
) |>
  layout(
    title = "OP-39 Breast Cancer Screening Recall Rates",
    xaxis = list(title = "Reported OP-39 percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of hospitals")
  )
```

## Compare median scores by state or territory

The state or territory median summarizes available hospital scores; it does not adjust for patient populations or clinical context and is not a ranking of care quality.

```{r}
mammography_by_state <- mammography_scores |>
  group_by(State) |>
  summarise(
    median_score = median(Score),
    hospitals = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(median_score)

plot_ly(
  data = mammography_by_state,
  x = ~median_score,
  y = ~reorder(State, median_score),
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  marker = list(color = "#d87850"),
  text = ~paste0("Hospitals with scores: ", hospitals),
  hovertemplate = "%{y}<br>Median: %{x:.1f}%<br>%{text}<extra></extra>"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Median OP-39 Score by State or Territory",
    xaxis = list(title = "Median reported percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "State or territory"),
    margin = list(l = 80),
    height = 950
  )
```

For measure specifications and source data, see the [CMS Outpatient Imaging Efficiency dataset](https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/wkfw-kthe).
